div.p: Volcano is a full-featured, standalone batch scheduling system built on top of Kubernetes. It was originally donated by Huawei and is now a CNCF incubating project.

button.aria-label: View source details for citation from Cloud Native Computing Foundation. Opens side panel.

p.span: Long-running training jobs, Big Data (Spark/Flink), and High-Performance Computing (HPC).

button.aria-label: View source details for citation from YouTube. Opens side panel.

li.p: Key Feature: Gang Scheduling. It treats a group of pods as a single "Job." It won't start any of them until there are enough resources for all of them.
How it works: It introduces a new "Job" custom resource (CRD). Instead of managing individual pods, you submit a VolcanoJob.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 558px; height: 1px; padding-top: 54px; margin-left: 747px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.p: Kueue (pronounced "Queue") is a newer, cloud-native job queueing controller. Unlike Volcano, which replaces the scheduling logic, Kueue acts as a gatekeeper that sits in front of the default scheduler.

button.aria-label: View source details for citation from Thoughtworks. Opens side panel.

li.p: Best For: Shared clusters with many teams, multi-cloud environments, and "Cloud Bursting."

p.span: It manages a global pool of resources (like "100 NVIDIA A100 GPUs") and decides which jobs are allowed to enter the cluster based on who has the remaining quota.

button.aria-label: View source details for citation from Medium. Opens side panel.

li.p: How it works: It puts your jobs in a "waitlist" (a ClusterQueue). Once the resources are free, it "admits" the job, and the standard Kubernetes scheduler then places the pods.

div.p: The Scenario: Team A submits a job needing 4 GPUs. Team B submits a job needing 4 GPUs. Your cluster only has 4 total.

li.p: Standard K8s: Might give 2 to Team A and 2 to Team B. Now both jobs are stuck waiting for the other 2 GPUs, but neither will ever finish.
Volcano/Kueue: Will give all 4 to Team A. Team A finishes quickly, then Team B gets the whole cluster. This results in much higher "Cluster Utilization."

div.p: Volcano excels in scenarios where a single "Job" has different types of pods that rely on each other to start.

Scenario: Distributed ML with a "Master" and "Worker" setup.
In a PyTorch training job, you often have one Master pod and multiple Worker pods.

li.p: The Problem: If you start the workers but the master pod fails the "Filtering Phase" because of a port conflict, the workers will sit idle forever.

Volcano's Solution: Volcano supports Task-level dependencies. It can be configured to say: "Only start the 100 Workers if, and only if, the Master pod is successfully placed." Standard Kubernetes (and therefore Kueue) doesn't understand these internal relationships between different pod types within the same job.

h3.span: Kueue excels in a corporate environment where multiple departments share a fixed, expensive resource pool (like 128 GPUs).

div.p:
Scenario: Departmental Quotas with "Resource Borrowing."
Imagine the Marketing Team has a quota of 10 GPUs and the Data Science Team has 50.

li.p: The Scenario: It’s Friday night. The Marketing Team is away, and their 10 GPUs are sitting idle. The Data Science team has a massive deadline and needs 60 GPUs.

Kueue's Solution: Kueue allows Resource Sharing/Borrowing. It can see that Marketing’s "Cohort" is empty and temporarily "lend" those 10 GPUs to Data Science. However, it also handles Preemption: if a Marketing person suddenly submits a job on Saturday morning, Kueue can automatically evict the "borrowed" Data Science job to give Marketing their guaranteed resources back.

p.span: Why not Volcano? Volcano is focused on the performance of the individual job, not the economic fairness and quota management across a multi-tenant organization.
